title: Constants
concept: In XIOM, let creates compile-time immutable bindings — values that never change, just like constants.
why: Immutable values make programs safer and easier to reason about. You know a value won't change unexpectedly.
syntax_ref: let CONSTANT_NAME = value;  // Immutable, never changes
tips: Use UPPER_CASE for constant names to signal they never change
`let` in XIOM is truly immutable — the compiler enforces it
Constants make your code's intent clear: 'this value is fixed'
common_mistakes: Trying to reassign a `let` — the compiler will reject it
Using `var` for values that never change — use `let` instead
Naming constants in lowercase — makes them hard to spot
